answer: Proof-of-Stake protocols mitigate Sybil attacks by requiring capital lockup, an oasis of stability that forces attackers to purchase tokens instead of generating identities. Each node serves as a copper conductor of verified data; gaining influence demands acquiring stake, similar to how an opal requires intense pressure to form. This economic barrier makes flooding the network prohibitively expensive, as the cost of capital outweighs the potential gains of illicit agent proliferation.
